condition: Welcome, course purpose and first-result preview, followed by named actions in Prework
scope: Ten synthetic personas × three standalone calls. Matched question, model and OS profiles across conditions. Cowork access and demonstrations described by the placeholders are assumed.
question:
Claude Desktop is already installed and your account has Cowork access. No course folder or previous course conversation exists. There is no trainer. You are trying this on your own.

Below is actual HTML from the handbook: navigation, cover, Start, contents and Prework, in their actual order. Cowork is selected; other runtime content is hidden and omitted. Initially closed panels show only their labels; their contents are available when opened. The Mac/Windows control starts on your computer's OS and can switch the setup directions. The rest of the handbook, including linked reading destinations, exists beyond this excerpt. Assess the start, not omitted later material. This is an HTML-reading simulation, not actual app execution or a visual screenshot test.

Based only on the HTML, describe what you would do, in order, until you could open and try the first game. Would you get going? How quick and obvious would that route feel to you? Report any hesitation, detour, need for help or reason to stop; if there is none, say so. Do not invent app behaviour or claim you executed anything.

Give a rating from 1.0 to 5.0 stars, in steps of 0.1. Keep these anchors: 1.0=cannot get going; 2.0=need substantial help; 3.0=can get going with detours; 4.0=clear with minor hesitation; 5.0=snappy and obvious throughout. Use values between anchors when they fit your experience better. Rate the route to the first visible result (the game), not full Prework completion or course quality. Report predicted getting going separately from smoothness.

Quote the instruction most relevant to your rating. Name the one change that would help you most, if any; none is allowed. Under 250 words. Return JSON with stars (number from 1.0 to 5.0 in steps of 0.1), wouldGetGoing (yes, no, or uncertain), firstActions (array), hesitations (array; empty if none), evidenceQuote (exact instruction text), feeling (your own voice), biggestImprovement (text; none if no change needed).

Where the HTML says to assume a video is here, assume the described demonstration is available. Do not invent content beyond its caption.

firstActions: Read the welcome: 'First, make a Snake game' with a preview image, and click the obvious 'Make my first game' link, which jumps to Prework.
Skim Prework and see the Mac/Windows toggle already on Mac. Watch the assumed short video showing the whole flow.
In Finder, open Documents and create an empty folder named agents-101.
Open Claude Desktop, start a new conversation, choose Cowork if offered, add the folder from the message box and select agents-101.
Wait until agents-101 shows as attached, then click Copy on the game prompt, paste it and send it. Approve if Claude asks, checking that it's writing into that folder.
When the agent says it's saved, open agents-101, then prework, and double-click snake.html to play in the browser.
hesitations: The start link scrolls to Prework, which opens with a general sentence about folders before the numbered steps. This is a small lag before the first action.
Step 1 is folder creation and Cowork setup under a heading about creating a folder. Skimming, I might miss that attaching the folder is part of that step.
'If you see a choice between Chat and Cowork' is vague. If I see neither, I would not know what to do.
Approval wording ('check that it's asking to make the game in that folder') is a little abstract for a non-technical user.
No time estimate is visible for the first game, so I can't tell whether it fits in my ten minutes.
judgements.evidenceQuote: Click Copy, paste the request into your task, and send it. The agent will make the prework folder and save the game inside it.
judgements.feeling: I'd get there. The 'Make my first game' link and the preview image hook me quickly, and the steps are short and in order. I'd skim past a couple of lines and wonder briefly whether I'd set up the folder correctly, but nothing would make me quit. The payoff is about five concrete steps away, which is fine for my ten minutes, though I'd like to be told how long it takes.
judgements.biggestImprovement: Have the 'Make my first game' link land directly on step 1 with a one-line summary and time estimate (for example, 'Make a folder, attach it in Cowork, paste one prompt: about 5 minutes'), so the first action is visible without reading the general Prework intro.
